topic: Serverless or containers: AWS Lambda vs Docker for your backend
caption:
Serverless or containers? It's one of the first backend decisions you'll make, and it shapes your hosting bill and your scaling. ☁️

The founder's version:

✅ Serverless (AWS Lambda) when traffic is spiky or unpredictable and you want to pay per request
✅ Containers (Docker) when you have steady traffic, long-running jobs or real-time connections
✅ Mixing both is normal: plenty of products run a container API with serverless jobs around it

Swipe for the details. →

slides.title: Serverless or containers for your backend?
slides.sub: It depends on your traffic and workload. Swipe →

cols.name: Serverless
cols.text: Functions like AWS Lambda run only when called. No servers to manage, scales on its own.

cols.name: Containers
cols.text: Your app packaged with Docker and kept running. More control, steady and predictable.

slides.title: Choose serverless when…
slides.body: traffic is spiky or unpredictable, tasks are short, and you'd rather not pay for servers sitting idle.

slides.title: Choose containers when…
slides.body: you have steady traffic, long-running jobs or real-time connections like live chat and tracking.

slides.title: Mixing both is normal.
slides.body: Many products run a container API with serverless jobs around it. Choose per workload, not per company.
